question: AITAT1 was established in 2024 to ensure accident investigations would be carried out with greater independence from the government and the authorities2. Article 22 of Directive (EU) 2016/798 lays down these bodies’ obligations in terms of independence3.

However, the chair of the AITAT and the board members responsible for the railway sector were appointed by the Council of Ministers, on the recommendation of Minister Óscar Puente. Only these senior officials hold the non-delegable power to approve technical accident investigation reports, and it is they who must either approve them or refer them back to the relevant technical investigation department4.
In the light of the above: 1.
Can the Commission confirm whether, as we understand, DG MOVE or the European Union Agency for Railways has received any warning or complaint regarding the possible lack of independence of the AITAT?
Has the Commission already assessed the independence of the AITAT by means of any specific checks?
Will it ask Pedro Sánchez’s Government for documented explanations and assurances that the Urda inquiry will examine facts and responsibilities without political interference?
